title: The builders started borrowing
sub: Hyperscaler bond issuance, US$ billions a year. 2020-24 is an AVERAGE, about $28B a year; 2025 actual; 2026 is an estimate range, $130-150B
src: Morgan Stanley IM; Mellon; Investing.com/LPL; PIMCO (via the evidence dossier)
src_full: 28: the hyperscalers' 2020-2024 ANNUAL AVERAGE bond issuance, drawn flat across 2020-2024 because it is one average, not five annual prints. 121: 2025 actual issuance (Mellon ~$121B; Morgan Stanley '>$100B'). 130 and 150: the two ends of the 2026 projected net supply range (+30-50%). All four are the dossier's secondary figures (Morgan Stanley IM, Mellon, Investing.com/LPL, PIMCO); none of those documents is on disk.

proof.quote: - **$28B** = the hyperscalers' **2020–2024 ANNUAL AVERAGE** bond issuance
Between 2020 and 2024, the biggest builders borrowed about twenty-eight billion dollars a year. Last year: a hundred and twenty-one billion. This year they're tracking toward a hundred and fifty.
